name: Oracle Rdb
tagline: DEC's relational database for OpenVMS, owned by Oracle since 1994 and still updated on Alpha and Itanium.
description: Oracle Rdb is the relational database Digital Equipment Corporation shipped in 1984 as VAX Rdb/VMS, and which Oracle bought in 1994. It runs only on OpenVMS, sits on the KODA storage kernel it shares with Oracle CODASYL DBMS, and is accessed through SQL, the older RDO language, precompilers or the SQL module language from COBOL, BASIC, Fortran and C programs. Rdb was known for one of the earliest cost-based optimizers and remains the standard upgrade path for OpenVMS applications built on RMS files. Despite a 2011 statement that 7.3 would be the last major version, Oracle keeps shipping 7.4.x updates: 7.4.1.5 arrived in January 2026 for OpenVMS on Alpha and Integrity (IA-64) servers, while an announced port to x86-64 OpenVMS has not appeared in current documentation.
statusNote: Still developed and supported by Oracle for OpenVMS Alpha and Itanium (7.4.1.5, January 2026); there is no confirmed x86-64 OpenVMS release.

pricing.notes: Licensed through Oracle with support contracts; pricing via Oracle sales.

scale.notes: Scales within OpenVMS clusters sharing the same disks; no sharding.

strengths: Four decades of stability in mission-critical OpenVMS shops
Natural upgrade path from RMS files for COBOL and BASIC applications
Runs across OpenVMS clusters with shared-disk access
Still receiving Oracle maintenance releases in 2026
Early pioneer of cost-based query optimisation
weaknesses: OpenVMS-only, and not yet available on x86-64 OpenVMS
Expensive licensing and a shrinking pool of skilled staff
Tied to ageing Alpha and Itanium hardware
useCases: Banking, manufacturing and government applications on OpenVMS clusters
Modernising RMS-file applications without leaving OpenVMS
notIdealFor: Any new platform choice outside OpenVMS
